session_covered: US and European sessions of Tuesday 29 September
intro: Covers the Tuesday 29 September US session. Sourcing caveat: the AFR's Before the Bell column and overnight SPI 200 data could not be accessed this morning; most figures come from a single aggregator (Trading Economics) and are flagged where they could not be cross-checked.
footnotes: NASDAQ Composite: the email showed 30,365.78 (+0.29%), far from the roughly 26,900-27,100 printed on the surrounding days, so it isn't shown.
VIX: the email gave "16.29 +0.22 pts (% not available)", which isn't a single figure, so it isn't shown in full.

Index, VIX, yield, AUD, Brent and gold levels are from Trading Economics and were not independently confirmed against a second closing-level source; the index figures are consistent with intraday direction reported by TheStreet (S&P 500 down, Nasdaq up, Dow down). Brent: TheStreet showed US$104.80 (-0.47%) mid-session versus US$102.52 (-2.62%) at Trading Economics; the latter is used as the later print. The iron ore print is for 28 September; 29 September was not available. VIX % change is not reported because the source's figure was internally inconsistent.

setup.summary: Overnight SPI 200 level and change: not available (only the day-session close, 8,722.0, -0.06%, was retrievable, which does not reflect the US session). Given a mixed US close (S&P 500 -0.14%, Nasdaq +0.29%), a small move either way at the open is the reasonable expectation, but no implied open is stated. The ASX 200 rose about 0.3% (about +30 points) on Tuesday; the closing level was reported as 8,697 and 8,709 in the same source, so the level is not available.

local_events: Market reaction to the RBA's 25 bp hike to 4.60% (announced 29 September) continues.
No other scheduled Australian releases were verified this morning.
what_moved: US equities lacked direction, with AI-related headlines the main focus and a Conference Board reading showing consumer confidence at a 12-year low. Treasury yields stayed near multi-year highs (10-year about 5.26%) on Fed hike expectations, while oil fell as US–Iran indirect talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and a new US emergency reserve release eased supply concerns. Industrials and technology led the S&P 500; energy lagged (sector percentages not available).

news.headline: RBA raises cash rate 25 bp to 4.60%.
news.summary: The unanimous decision cited materialising inflation risks from Middle East energy effects, AI-driven technology prices and domestic capacity pressure; the Board said demand growth needs to stay subdued for a period.

news.headline: US consumer confidence falls to a 12-year low.
news.summary: The weak reading weighed on the S&P 500 and small caps (Russell 2000 down about 0.7% intraday).

news.headline: Oil eases on Hormuz diplomacy and reserve release.
news.summary: US and Iranian officials held separate indirect talks via mediators; the US will offer up to 40 million barrels from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve (bids due 6 October) and Saudi Arabia has restored about half its pipeline capacity.

news.headline: Treasury yields stay near multi-year highs.
news.summary: The 10-year is at 5.26%, up about 51 bp over the past month, with markets pricing roughly a 70% chance of a Fed hike by October (Fed funds now 3.75%-4.00%).

news.headline: Gold rebounds from a seven-week low.
news.summary: Spot gold rose 1.34% to about US$4,170/oz but is down about 6% over the month on rate-hike pricing.

news.headline: AI headlines dominate US tech trading.
news.summary: Nvidia authorised a record US$150 billion buyback and AMD agreed an US$8.2 billion acquisition, while reports of an Anthropic IPO prospectus and a White House meeting on AI safety kept sentiment focused on the sector.

news.headline: ASX 200 edges higher ahead of the RBA.
news.summary: The index gained about 0.3% on Tuesday but is down about 4.2% over the past month.

coming_up: US ADP employment and the PCE price index are due Wednesday 30 September (US time); ISM Manufacturing on Thursday 1 October; and the September US jobs report on Friday 2 October. PCE and payrolls are the releases most likely to shape October Fed hike expectations.
